kosala.notes: MN 116:6.6 names the paccekabuddha between two other buddhas. Sujato spells his name Kosala, but the Pāli kosallo has its own DPD sense, kosalla 3, outside this packet. All 89 listed discourses refer to the land, its people or King Pasenadi of Kosala. The packet misses the kingdom in the lists of sixteen countries in AN 3.70, 8.42, 8.43 and 8.45, where the English list is one segment earlier than the Pāli. It also misses Pasenadi’s designation in AN 6.43, MN 87, SN 3.3–7, 3.12, 3.17–18, 3.23–24 and Ud 2.9, where it is omitted in translation, and the recap at AN 5.50:20.4. The Sundarikā river episode is at Snp 3.4:1.2, while the citation maps to Snp 3.6. Several page references also pick up adjacent discourses, e.g. AN 5.29 beside the actual Icchānaṅgala setting in AN 5.30.

kosambī.notes: The departure from Kosambī, the Ganges bank and the rosewood grove are in SN 22.81, 35.241 and 56.31 respectively. Their page references also pick up SN 22.80, 35.240 and 56.30. Kosambī appears in the Pāli recaps at MN 50:32.3 (kosambi) and SN 12.70:30.5, both outside the packet’s list.

kosiya.notes: The Buddha in DN 21, Moggallāna in MN 37 and Mahākassapa in Ud 3.7 all address Sakka by his clan name. The citation of Thag 6.7 concerns Kātiyāna, addressed as indasagotta (of Indra’s clan). Thag 5.12:5.5 explicitly credits the elder Kosiya with the five verses.

koṇḍañña.notes: DN 14:1.6 gives Koṇḍañña as the clan of Vipassī, Sikhī and Vessabhū. SN 56.11:11.1 names the disciple Koṇḍañña and 14.3 explains his name Aññāsikoṇḍañña. The packet has no biographical entry for him or for the earlier Buddha of that name.

koṭigāma.notes: SN 56.21:1.1 places the village among the Vajjis. Check the entry’s location for Ambapālī’s meal and the Licchavis’ visit. In DN 16 the Buddha leaves Koṭigāma for Ñātika (2.5), reaches Vesālī (2.11), and meets Ambapālī and the Licchavis there (2.14–19).

kukkula.notes: MN 130:21.1–22.1 puts the Hell of Burning Chaff between the Dung Hell and the silk-cotton forest, exactly as in the entry. Its Pāli compound kukkulaniraya has a separate DPD line, which accounts for the absence of this passage from the packet’s tap list. At SN 10.5:9–10 Sānu’s mother uses hot coals as an image for returning to sensual pleasures.

kukkuṭārāma.notes: AN 5.50 places Nārada at the monastery in Pāṭaliputta. Dasama visits it in MN 52 and AN 11.16, and Ānanda and Bhadda stay there in SN 45.18. The page references also pick up AN 5.49, AN 11.15, MN 51 and SN 45.15–17.

kumārakassapa.notes: AN 1.217 names him as foremost in brilliant speech. The page reference also picks up AN 1.198–208 and 1.219–234. Thag 2.41:2.7 attributes the verses to him. His name in Thag 2.49:3.1 belongs to the chapter recap after Sandhita’s verses.
